title: A20 inhibits pyroptosis in cisplatin-resistant breast cancer via regulating NLRP3
content:
Abstract
Background
Breast cancer (BC) frequently develops resistance to cisplatin (DDP), limiting therapeutic efficacy. Pyroptosis, a form of inflammatory programmed cell death, has been implicated in chemoresistance, but its regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. A20, a deubiquitinating enzyme, is often dysregulated in cancers.
Objective
This study aimed to investigate whether A20 modulates pyroptosis to promote DDP resistance in BC and explore its underlying mechanism.
Methods
DDP-resistant MCF-7/DDP and MDA-MB-231/DDP cells were established via chronic DDP exposure, and the resistance phenotype was verified by comparing the half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) values and resistance indices of the resistant cells with those of the parental cells. Cell viability, proliferation, and pyroptosis were assessed using cell counting kit-8, colony formation, and flow cytometry assays, and pyroptosis was further corroborated by a lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release assay. A20 and NOD-like receptor family, pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3) expression was evaluated via reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) and Western blot. Bioinformatics analysis of the GSE103115 dataset identified differentially expressed genes linked to chemoresistance.
Results
DDP-resistant cells exhibited higher A20 expression than parental cells. A20 silencing suppressed cell viability and proliferation, and promoted pyroptosis. NLRP3 is an important downstream target of A20 in MCF-7/DDP and MDA-MB-231/DDP cells. NLRP3 silencing partially reversed the effects of A20 silencing on cell viability, proliferation, and pyroptosis in MCF-7/DDP and MDA-MB-231/DDP cells.
Conclusion
A20 inhibited pyroptosis in DDP-resistant BC via regulating NLRP3, suggesting A20 as a potential therapeutic target to overcome chemoresistance.
Insight
Our study revealed that A20 promoted DDP resistance in BC by inhibiting NLRP3-mediated pyroptosis. These findings establish a novel mechanism linking A20 dysregulation to chemoresistance and highlight pyroptosis as a critical node in BC therapy. Targeting A20 or restoring NLRP3-dependent pyroptosis may offer new strategies to overcome DDP resistance.
